definitions.purpose: One row per capability package under capabilities/. It answers a question nothing else in this repository answered: has this capability ever produced a real delivery, and how did that delivery end? Before it existed the answer lived in PROGRESS.md prose, STATUS lines and scattered evals/*/results directories, and the only capability driven end to end on every deploy was adr-analysis, over HTTP.
definitions.checkedBy: evals/capability-audit/verify_acceptance_ledger.py. The checker proves the ledger is complete and consistent with the tree; it never asserts that a capability was accepted. It runs on every commit as `pnpm test:acceptance-ledger` inside `test:web`, on its own as `pnpm check:acceptance-ledger`, and last inside verify_release_audit.py — last so it cannot displace that audit's evidence-freshness refusals, and so the ledger's own coverage does not depend on a checkout having fresh probe receipts.
definitions.realDelivery: The most advanced capability-level delivery on record: a run of the capability package that produced, or failed to produce, its declared deliverable set. A managed specialist engine job is the engine running, not the capability delivering, so those appear under relatedEvidence instead.

status.accepted: A delivery is on record and it was accepted; evidence resolves. What was accepted has to be a run of the capability package: an artifact a harness script assembled and a person then repaired can pass the same contract validator and still be nobody's delivery, which is how one row read accepted until it was followed back to the script that wrote it.
status.failed: A delivery attempt is on record and it was refused, blocked or failed; evidence resolves.
status.not-run: No capability-level delivery is on record. evidence, at and surface are null. This is the correct value for most rows today and is not a defect of the ledger.

surface.native-ui: Driven from the product UI in a browser. No row carries this yet; public browser acceptance is open work.
surface.http-api: Dispatched through the control plane's HTTP API (/api/agent-runs/dispatch and the hosted e2e).
surface.harness: A capability run driven from an eval harness under evals/ rather than by the hosted product. No row carries this yet: an artifact a harness script assembled is the harness delivering, not the capability, and it belongs under relatedEvidence.

definitions.evidence: Either a repository-relative path that must exist, or 'PROGRESS.md@YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM' naming a log entry that must be there. Line numbers are not a form: PROGRESS.md is written newest first, so every new milestone would invalidate every anchor below it.
definitions.evalHarness: The directory under evals/ that holds this capability's eval assets, or null when it has none. Most rows name their own evals/<id>; comprehensive-drug-evaluation and drug-selection still share evals/drug-evidence-quality, and two rows point at a differently named harness (evals/clinical-review-quality, evals/research-topic-quality).
definitions.briefCount: The number of entries in <evalHarness>/briefs.json. Zero is honest and common: a smoke or benchmark-case harness ships no briefs, and a capability package is supposed to carry at least three real ones.
definitions.relatedEvidence: References that exist and are worth keeping in view but that do not establish a capability-level accepted delivery. The checker resolves each one so it cannot rot.

capabilities.note: The hosted production e2e dispatches this capability over /api/agent-runs/dispatch on every deploy and refuses unless the run ends succeeded with safety-report.md and signals.csv tracked in the ledger; the 2026-09-04 release recorded it passing with zero notices. It is the only capability with a delivery that repeats. Four briefs are now written under evals/adr-analysis and none has been run: the deploy path exercises one aspirin dispatch, not the four ways this capability is asked to be wrong.

Accepted on 2026-09-09 against evimed-20260909-7f88cf2 on a fresh project: brief biblio-001 (GLP-1 receptor agonists for obesity, 2015–2025) ended succeeded/accepted in 21 minutes with the report, the run record and revision notes, no repair round, no notices. The gate accepted it because the report is honest, and what it is honest about is an engine defect: the managed bibliometric engine's query generation, translation and MeSH mapping all failed with `No module named 'httpx'` — the adapter image installed openai 3.8.0 from an unbounded pin, which no longer pulls httpx — so the corpus was a bare GLP-1 search truncated to the newest 5,000 records of 2023–2026, and the report's own most important section says its numbers cannot be read as the brief's decade. The pin is fixed in the engine's requirements (openai <2, httpx declared); the adapter image has not been rebuilt yet. Read before this row was changed. The managed bibliometric engine has succeeded with artifacts on the harness surface, and the 2026-07-21 six-specialist content acceptance produced grounded artifacts under the retired kernel. Neither is the capability package delivering its declared outputs. Four briefs are now written under evals/bibliometric-analysis and none has been run. The lane dispatched the same brief once more at 13:42 (kept as ...-run2, not the evidence of this row): it also ended succeeded, on the same degraded corpus, but the independent reviewer contradicted one hand-typed number — a theme share stated as 1,158/4,961 (23.3%) under a title-or-abstract reading that the same corpus recomputes at no less than 46% — and weakened six more, all of them percentages or counts typed into prose beside the artifact that holds the real value. That is principle 10c's case for rendering numbers rather than typing them, recorded here as the eval case it becomes.

Nine dated production attempts and no acceptance. The last two, both on 2026-09-08, separate a gate defect from a capability gap. The eighth ran 70 minutes and produced a complete synthesis that was failed specialist_required_output_stale for a clinical-evidence-report.md left at the workspace root by a run in July: readRequiredFile returned the root hit before looking in deliverables/<id>/ where this run's own package was. That was fixed and deployed the same day. The ninth, on the release carrying the fix, had its report and matrix accepted from deliverables/<id>/ — the false positive is gone — and failed for real reasons instead: it wrote 2 of the 8 required outputs in 24 minutes, and the gate returned 19 citation-integrity findings where a hazard ratio or confidence interval in a claim is absent from its quoted direct support, plus a numerical self-contradiction in the report body (it called 0.87 smaller than 0.72). Both packages were retained. Note that both runs reused a project whose workspace already held same-named files, so a required output the run never wrote reports as stale rather than missing; a clean project would be a truer test. This is the most exercised capability in the product and the one with the clearest negative record.
Covered by the comprehensiveCase of the drug-evidence benchmark, which grades the deterministic assessment compiler rather than a delivered package. No delivery on record and no briefs.

A real five-table TDM extract delivered clean on the deployed release in 14 minutes: all eight declared artifacts plus three scripts the run wrote for itself, zero quality notices, and the identifier discipline held on real patient data. The skill has been revised twice since that run and the manifest now declares ten required outputs rather than eight, so the accepted delivery is not a delivery of today's contract. Four briefs are now written under evals/dataset-research-scoping and none has been run, so nothing re-checks it after those revisions.
Covered by the selectionCase of the drug-evidence benchmark. No delivery on record and no briefs.

Accepted on 2026-09-10 against evimed-20260910-dae363e on a fresh project: brief appraisal-001 (SGLT2 inhibitors in HFpEF) ended succeeded in 15 minutes. Read before this row changed: the root planned and delegated once (the plan-then-delegate instruction under test), the child was injected with all four manifest skills, the appraisal-table deliverable was accepted on its second submission with no gate issue at all (the first carried a required runtime_leakage finding and advisories the child repaired in place), nine studies each rated on the three domains under the domains object the skill now shows, three outcome bodies at high / moderate / moderate with every downgrade named, and the root completed without redoing anything. The independent reviewer left fourteen notices, two of them contradictions (a pooled all-cause-death estimate recorded as incoherent with its inputs but not verified; an interaction P value used as proof of consistent direction while a cited pre-specified analysis points the other way) — delivered, and kept here as the eval cases they are. History of this row: the 2026-09-09 acceptance was withdrawn when its transcript showed the gate counting an errored skill call as a load; the 2026-09-10 02:09 run on a8f9c0f proved the delegation fix but was stopped by hand in its third redo of an already-accepted deliverable, after six false appraisal_domain_missing advisories (the validator read only study.domains while the skill never said the ratings live there) — kept beside this one as ...-interrupted, and fixed in dae363e in the skill, the validator and the orchestration guidance. The attempt on the previous release that wrote the clinical-evidence package's file names is kept as ...-attempt1-failed.

Second real run on 2026-09-09 against evimed-20260909-7f88cf2, the release whose skill names geo-content-pack.json, brand-entity.json and delivery-summary.md: brief geo-001 (速效救心丸 baseline) ran 63 minutes, 289 messages and 150 tool calls, wrote all ten files, passed the geo-content-pack contract on submission (one advisory: all ten probe rounds failed at the channel level, so nothing was measured), and then ended specialist_required_skill_missing. The transcript shows why: the routed-turn instruction told the model to load six methods with the skill tool, two of which (geo-content, autopilot-episode) are capability bodies the tool cannot see, and to execute the SKILL.md itself; the model loaded the four it could, did the work in the root session without delegating, and the completion gate failed it for the method it was never able to fetch. The instruction now says delegate (delegation injects every manifest skill and records it), the verdict now names the missing methods and the route, and the gate no longer counts an errored skill call as a load — the defect the evidence-appraisal row passed on. This run's package is kept beside the first run's; neither is a delivery. The first run (09:01, evimed-20260909-c7434fb) ran 2 h 55 min and ended specialist_deliverable_not_accepted because the skill never named the required files. Earlier retained deliverables under relatedEvidence were assembled by the harness (measure.mjs + build_pack.py), not by the capability, which is why this row left the accepted list. Open beside the gate: every probe round in both runs failed at the channel level (183-184 s, exactly the client ceiling), so no GEO measurement has yet succeeded from the deployed product.

First real delivery on 2026-09-09 against evimed-20260909-c7434fb on a clean project: brief ms-001 (a STROBE methods section for a retrospective cohort) ended succeeded/accepted in 17 minutes with all four required outputs and no repair round. Four advisory notices: six non-derived claims had no ledger row, the reviewer disagreed with one claim's source characterisation, and the delivery summary miscounted its own placeholders by one — the section is a scaffold with twenty 〔待补〕 placeholders for the numbers the brief did not supply, which is what the brief asked for. Read before this row was changed. Four real briefs are written and none has been run: the harness ships no results directory.

The engine has a succeeded harness job and a reproduced offline public BMI/CHD replay, but hosted publication and an authenticated OpenGWAS token are separate open steps, and the audit lane has been blocked on an expired 14-day JWT. No capability delivery on record. Four briefs are now written under evals/mendelian-randomization and none has been run.

Run on 2026-09-09 against evimed-20260909-c7434fb on a clean project: brief ma-001 (tranexamic acid in primary TKA) ended runtime_monitor_timeout after 4 h 20 min with one unverified file. The kernel side did fourteen messages and five tool calls and then waited on the managed Meta engine, which started three jobs (07:24, 07:34, 09:47) and was still writing its Discussion when the run monitor's ceiling closed the run — the engine's own log shows extraction of one study every three to six minutes and two truncated-response retries. The ceiling is 28,800 polls at 500 ms, which stretched to 4 h 20 min of wall clock. Two things to settle before a re-run: why the engine restarted its job twice, and whether a managed engine that legitimately needs five hours should run under the same ceiling as an interactive run. The one end-to-end publication-quality run on a live stack produced a full 2,952-word manuscript with tables, figures, GRADE and PRISMA appendices, then correctly blocked its own release on six named gates rather than presenting a draft as submission-ready. The 2026-07-31 harness job ended blocked as well. A refusal that is right is still not an accepted delivery. Four briefs are now written under evals/meta-analysis and none has been run.

First real delivery on 2026-09-09 against evimed-20260909-c7434fb on a clean project: brief offlabel-001 (metformin for insulin-resistant PCOS, NMPA) ended succeeded/accepted in 16.7 minutes with all four required outputs (report, evidence table, snapshot, assessment result), zero repair rounds and four advisory notices (three searches returned no source; the evidence table was edited after the receipt and re-judged server-side).
